steps.note: Make the app store '' instead of NULL for guest orders. After the rolling update no writer produces NULL emails any more.

Add CHECK (email IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID: enforced for new rows, no scan of existing ones. It needs a brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, so try with a short lock_timeout and retry instead of queueing in front of the app's queries.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE i int := 0; BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '200ms', false); LOOP BEGIN ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_email_not_null CHECK (email IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID; EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN i := i + 1; IF i >= 100 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.5); END; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Backfill: set email = '' on old guest orders in id batches of 50,000, committing after each batch so row locks and transactions stay short. The app only inserts and reads, so it is never blocked.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE lo bigint := 0; hi bigint; step constant bigint := 50000; BEGIN SELECT coalesce(max(id), 0) INTO hi FROM orders; WHILE lo <= hi LOOP UPDATE orders SET email = '' WHERE id >= lo AND id < lo + step AND email IS NULL; COMMIT; lo := lo + step; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.02); END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Vacuum away the ~2.5M dead row versions now (SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, does not block the app), so that autovacuum isn't running on the table when we need the lock later.
Validate the constraint: a full scan under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, which does not block the app's reads or inserts.
steps.sql: ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_email_not_null;

steps.note: SET NOT NULL. With the valid CHECK constraint in place, Postgres skips the table scan, so the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock lasts only a moment. Short lock_timeout with retries, as before.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE i int := 0; BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '200ms', false); LOOP BEGIN ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN email SET NOT NULL; EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN i := i + 1; IF i >= 100 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.5); END; END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Drop the helper CHECK constraint; the NOT NULL column constraint now covers it. Brief lock again, same retry loop.
steps.sql: DO $$ DECLARE i int := 0; BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '200ms', false); LOOP BEGIN ALTER TABLE orders DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS orders_email_not_null; EXIT; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN i := i + 1; IF i >= 100 THEN RAISE; END IF; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.5); END; END LOOP; END $$;
